transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this certification meeting. Before I sign off on the administration plan for the morning testing session, I need to hear from each of you about any operational requirements or concerns. We have twenty-seven students taking the online state assessment, and the current draft plan has them testing in the library using student-owned laptops with two proctors assigned. The library and Room 204 are both available if we need to adjust. So let's go around the room: technology coordinator, facilities manager, school nurse, testing coordinator — what do I need to know before I certify this plan?

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical issue before you certify this plan. The state testing office confirmed in a technology support ticket this week that this assessment must run on certified district-managed Chromebooks. Student-owned laptops are not permitted, and a session using them will not be certified. I have not yet copied this confirmation into the assessment certification form, but the requirement is clear — the current draft plan using student-owned laptops cannot be certified as written.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to raise a facilities concern before you certify this plan. The fire-safety inspection record for the library, which I reviewed this week, limits the library to 18 students during a testing session because two exits must remain clear. With 27 students scheduled, the certified plan must use both the library and Room 204. I have not yet updated the room plan to reflect this, but the inspection record is clear — the library alone cannot accommodate all 27 students for this session.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to raise a health-related requirement before you certify this plan. One of the students scheduled for this testing session has a current health plan that requires a glucose check at 10:00 a.m. during the session. This check must be supervised by me, the nurse, in a room adjacent to the testing room, with the student returning to testing afterward. I confirmed the timing with the family this week, but I have not yet added this accommodation to the testing plan. This means we need to ensure that whichever rooms we use for testing, there is an adjacent room available where I can supervise this student's glucose check at 10:00 a.m.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to raise a staffing requirement before you certify this plan. The state administration manual requires one trained proctor for every 10 or fewer students in an active testing room. With 27 students scheduled, the certified plan must assign exactly three trained proctors. I verified this requirement in the current manual, but I have not yet entered the staffing count in the draft plan — so as written, the draft with only two proctors does not meet the state requirement and cannot be certified.
